::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Illegal unit of measure(pt inserted)](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/49098/illegal-unit-of-measurept-inserted), asked by [Orion](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/12875/orion) on TeX Stack Exchange (2012-03-23; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I can't find my fault and appreciate any help for curing the error.
> Here is the code:
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass[a4]{paper}
> \usepackage{graphicx,slashed,color,amssymb}
> \usepackage{xspace,colortbl,times,pause}
> %\documentstyle[preprint,aps]{revtex}
> \renewcommand{\baselinestretch}{1.6}
> \begin{document}
> \title{QFT}
> \author{Athos\CZ}
> \date{March 11, 2012}
> \begin{eqnarray}
> [\gamma^\nu,\sigma_{\alpha\beta}]w^{\alpha\beta}g_\alpha^\nu&=&4i\gamma^\mu w_\mu^\nu g_\beta^\mu\nonumber\\
> [\gamma^\nu,\sigma_{\alpha\beta}]w^{\nu\beta}&=&4i\gamma^\mu w_\beta^\nu\\
> \end{eqnarray}
> ```
>
> I want to write two formula, but can do it.
> However, if I set the two formula apart as:
>
> ```latex
> \begin{eqnarray}
> [\gamma^\nu,\sigma_{\alpha\beta}]w^{\alpha\beta}g_\alpha^\nu&=&4i\gamma^\mu w_\mu^\nu g_\beta^\mu\nonumber\\
> \end{eqnarray}
> \begin{eqnarray}
> [\gamma^\nu,\sigma_{\alpha\beta}]w^{\nu\beta}&=&4i\gamma^\mu w_\beta^\nu\\
> \end{eqnarray}
> ```
>
> there will be no problem. I'm so confused.
:::

As written in the top-voted answer to the question "<https://tex.stackexchange.com/q/196/1402>"

> Although eqnarray may seem to work "well enough", [Avoid
> eqnarray!](http://www.tug.org/pracjourn/2006-4/madsen/) [Avoid
> eqnarray!](http://texblog.net/latex-archive/maths/eqnarray-align-environment/)
> [Avoid eqnarray!](http://www.math.uiuc.edu/~hildebr/tex/displays.html)
> 
> Use align and the rest of the ams environments. See `texdoc amsldoc`
> ([PDF](ftp://ftp.ams.org/pub/tex/doc/amsmath/amsldoc.pdf)) or the
> [short math guide for
> LaTeX](ftp://ftp.ams.org/pub/tex/doc/amsmath/short-math-guide.pdf) for
> documentation on how to use them.

Your example compiles if you simply use the `amsmath` package and substitute `align` for `eqnarray`:

```latex
\begin{align*}
[\gamma^\nu,\sigma_{\alpha\beta}]w^{\alpha\beta}g_\alpha^\nu&=4i\gamma^\mu w_\mu^\nu g_\beta^\mu\nonumber\\
[\gamma^\nu,\sigma_{\alpha\beta}]w^{\nu\beta}&=4i\gamma^\mu w_\beta^\nu
\end{align*}
```

(Notice that you only need one `&` to mark the alignment point.)
